chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, who said:

I had carried merchandise to Mecca, but losses occurred upon it, so I entered the city with it to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I carried merchandise that incurred losses upon me, and I have resolved to travel to Egypt, so shall I travel by land or by sea?' He said, 'Egypt is the place of death; shortest-lived people are destined for it.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'How beautiful is the seeking for one who sails the sea.'

Then he said to me, 'It is not against you if you go to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), pray two cycles there, and ask Allah for guidance (Istikhara) a hundred times. Whatever is resolved for you, act upon it.'
So if you ride by land, say: 'All praise is for Allah Who made this subservient to us, and we were not able to do it, and surely to our Lord we must return.'
And if you sail the sea, when you are in the ship, say: 'In the Name of Allah, its course and its anchorage. Surely my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.'

So if the waves heave upon you, lean on your left side and gesture towards the wave with your right hand, and say: 'Settle me with the settling of Allah, and be tranquil with the tranquility of Allah, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent.'
Ali ibn Asbaat said, 'So I sailed the sea, and whenever the wave rose, I would say what he had said, and it would subside as if it had not been.'

Ali ibn Asbaat said, 'And I asked him, saying, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the tranquility (Sakinah)?' He said, 'A wind from Paradise, having a face like the face of a human, more fragrant than musk. And it is that which Allah sent down upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at Hunayn, so the polytheists were defeated.'

key_terms.السَّكِينَةُ: Tranquility/Sakinah, explained here as a fragrant wind from Paradise
key_terms.حُنَيْنٌ: Hunayn, a location associated with a divine wind during the Prophet's time
key_terms.مِصْرُ الْحُتُوفِ: Egypt, described as the place of death/destiny

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and rituals for safe sea travel according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical jurisprudence of travel (*safar*) in Shia tradition, where Imam Al-Rida (AS) not only advises on the safer mode of transport but also prescribes specific *istikhara* (guidance prayer) rituals to align one's will with divine decree. The explanation of *Sakinah* as a personified, fragrant wind from Paradise sent at Hunayn connects this narrative to broader eschatological and historical themes of divine assistance (*tawfiq*) in overcoming adversity, reinforcing the spiritual dimension of worldly endeavors.
